senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; עָנָה II)humility, lowliness, meekness, kindness.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:15">Sot. IX, 15</cite> (<cite ref="Sotah 49a:16">49ᵃ</cite>) <he>משמת רבי בטלה ע׳ וכ׳</he> with Rabbi’s death ceased humility and fear of sin. Ib. 49ᵇ <he>לא תיתני ע׳ דאיכא אנא</he> do not read (in the Mishnah) ‘humility’, for there am I (striving after it).

<cite ref="Arakhin 16b:34">Arakh. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>ע׳ שלא לשמה</he> humility not for its own sake (e.g. you forbear to rebuke a friend, making yourself believe that you are unworthy to do so, whereas in fact you only fear to incur your friend’s ill will). Y. Shek. II, end, 47ᶜ <he>קדושה מביאה לידי ע׳ ע׳ מביאה לידי יראת חטא</he> holiness leads to meekness, meekness leads to fear of sin; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 20b:11">Ab. Zar. 20ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 20b:11">Ib.</cite> <he>ע׳ גדולה מכולן</he> humility is the greatest virtue of all.
<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 7:2">Ab. d’R. N. ch. VII</cite> <he>למד בני ביתך ע׳</he> (not <he>למוד</he>) train the members of thy household to be kind (to strangers).

<cite ref="Tractate Derekh Eretz Zuta 5:4">Der. Er. Zutta, ch. V</cite> <he>הדר חכמה ע׳ הדר ע׳ יראה</he> the beauty of wisdom is modesty, the beauty of modesty is fear of sin. Tanḥ. Bresh. 1; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:3:11">Y. Sabb. I, 3ᶜ</cite> top, a. e., v. <cite ref="O00318"><he>סוּלְיָיס</he></cite>; a. fr.
